title: Weather-Robust Cross-View Geo-Localization via Prototype-Based Semantic Part Discovery
claim: A shared backbone feeds three complementary readouts that fuse into one embedding for matching, with training-only objectives kept separate.
layout: 5 numbered panels, left-to-right top row, training objectives strip below
description: A wide, numbered five-stage diagram with dashed rounded panels. The top row reads left to right. (1) Inputs: stacked drone and satellite aerial images. (2) Tokenization: a shared DINOv2 ViT-S/14 token column, with a CLS token and a patch grid. (3) The largest panel splits into three tinted bands: pink Global CLS, yellow Parts (prototype dots, pooling, altitude FiLM note) and green Layout (a two-layer graph attention network over part nodes). Arrows labeled w_c, w_p and w_g converge on a circular Feature Fusion gate, which outputs a colored 768-D embedding bar. (4) Cross-view Matching: a sphere with the query and satellite tiles, an angle θ, and the note 'rank gallery by cos θ'. A bottom strip, panel 5, shows four training objectives in small mini-diagrams: alignment, part quality, teacher distillation and altitude adaptation. Pastel colors group the branches, and the eye goes first to the central three-branch fusion.
caption: \textbf{\ours{} overview.} (1--2) A shared DINOv2 ViT-S/14 tokenizes the drone query and the satellite tile into a CLS token and patch tokens. (3) The head reads the tokens in three ways: the global CLS token; a part branch in which patch tokens are assigned by cosine similarity to $K_{\max}{=}12$ learnable prototypes and pooled into $f_part$; and a two-layer GAT over the active prototypes that encodes their spatial layout. Altitude conditions the part branch through FiLM during training only; at test time FiLM uses its mean parameters and needs no altitude input. A fusion gate with weights $w_c, w_p, w_g$ combines the three readouts into one $\ell_2$-normalized 768-D embedding. (4) Retrieval is a single cosine ranking of the satellite gallery. (5) The four Kendall-weighted loss groups (alignment, part quality, teacher distillation, altitude) are used only during training.
abstract: The low-altitude economy is growing rapidly, increasing demand for reliable drone navigation. Common tasks such as delivery, inspection, and search-and-rescue rely on Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS), which can be jammed, spoofed, or unavailable. Cross-view geo-localization (CVGL), which matches an oblique drone view to a geo-referenced satellite tile, offers an alternative for autonomous localization when GNSS fails. However, current CVGL methods have three limitations: (1) global descriptors compress patch grids into a single vector, without separating cross-view-shared layout from view-specific texture; (2) altitude-related scale variation remains in the learned embedding instead of being marginalized as a nuisance; and (3) multi-objective training uses hand-tuned loss weights despite incompatible gradient scales. We propose SKYPART, a lightweight, swappable head for patch-based vision transformers (ViTs) that explicitly groups patches into parts. It combines (i) learnable prototypes that compete for patch tokens through single-pass cosine assignment; (ii) altitude-conditioned linear modulation used only during training, yielding altitude-free retrieval embeddings at inference; (iii) graph-attention readout over active prototypes; and (iv) Kendall uncertainty-weighted multi-objective learning that learns loss-group weights end-to-end. With 26.95M parameters and 22.14 GFLOPs, SKYPART is the smallest top-performing method in our comparison and achieves state-of-the-art results on SUES-200, University-1652, and DenseUAV using single-pass retrieval without reranking or test-time augmentation (TTA). Its accuracy advantage over the strongest baseline further increases under ten WeatherPrompt corruption conditions. Code: https://github.com/chisngyen/SkyPart.
